fixes.find: No published price book, no membership plan, no financing. Those are real gaps against the franchises and we are not going to invent them here.
fixes.replace: City & Suburban does not publish a price book. It diagnoses before any quote and gives an upfront written price before work, with no hidden fees. Maintenance plan members get priority dispatch, and financing is available through Wells Fargo Home Projects, subject to credit approval.
fixes.why: CRITICAL 1: false denial of membership plan and financing

fixes.find: We do not publish a membership plan. Customers schedule seasonal visits directly and reviewers describe that as easy to arrange. If a published plan matters to you, that is a genuine gap against the larger franchises and you should weigh it.
fixes.replace: Yes. City & Suburban offers a maintenance plan, and plan members get priority dispatch. Seasonal service on both heating and cooling is worthwhile on equipment the owner intends to keep. Before joining, it is worth asking which equipment the plan covers and getting the plan terms in writing.
fixes.why: CRITICAL 2: false denial of the maintenance plan

fixes.find: Do you offer a maintenance plan?
fixes.replace: Does City & Suburban offer a maintenance plan?
fixes.why: MAJOR 16: second-person FAQ question

fixes.find: Heating and cooling, quoted by the same person who will do the work. Tell us what you have and what it is doing.
fixes.replace: Heating and cooling, diagnosed before any quote, with an upfront written price before work begins. Describe the equipment and what it is doing.
fixes.why: CRITICAL 3: universal same-person delivery promise

fixes.find: Both trades, same company, same person quoting. You are not coordinating two contractors around one basement.
fixes.replace: City & Suburban works on both heating and cooling, so a problem that spans the furnace, the air conditioner and a shared blower or thermostat can be diagnosed by one company rather than two contractors working around one basement.
fixes.why: CRITICAL 3: same-person quoting promise

fixes.find: Yes. That is the point of this page - one firm, one person quoting, no coordinating two contractors around the same basement and the same thermostat.
fixes.replace: Yes. City & Suburban works on both heating and cooling equipment, so a problem involving a shared blower, control board or thermostat can be diagnosed by one company rather than split between two contractors.
fixes.why: CRITICAL 3: same-person quoting promise; answer was truncated to 'Yes.'

fixes.find: Do you handle both the heating and the cooling side?
fixes.replace: Does City & Suburban handle both the heating and the cooling side?

fixes.find: If you are holding a quote from someone else, send it. We will tell you if it is fair.

fixes.find: We will tell you if the quote you have is fair. Sometimes it is
fixes.replace: Proposed equipment, sizing and scope checked against the home
fixes.why: CRITICAL 4: general quote-fairness promise in pricing row

fixes.find: Yes, and sometimes we tell people the quote they are holding is a fair one. A reviewer who called us as a second opinion was told their unit still had life and to come back when it did not.
fixes.replace: Yes. City & Suburban can discuss the scope of a quote from another contractor, starting with its own diagnosis of the equipment. A useful second opinion checks the proposed sizing, matched equipment, venting and permit responsibility, and sometimes confirms that the existing quote is reasonable or that repair is the better path.
fixes.why: CRITICAL 4: single review turned into a general promise

fixes.find: Can you give a second opinion on a quote I already have?
fixes.replace: Can City & Suburban give a second opinion on an existing quote?
fixes.why: MAJOR 16: second-person FAQ question

fixes.find: If both are near end of life, yes - one visit, matched coil and condenser, correct staging, and you pay for one installation rather than two. If only one is failing, we will tell you. Several reviewers were told to replace one and keep the other.
fixes.replace: Often, if both are near end of life: one installation, a matched coil and condenser, and correct staging. If only one is failing, replacing that one and keeping the other can be the better call. City & Suburban diagnoses before any quote and gives an upfront written price before work, so the recommendation rests on the condition of each system.
fixes.why: MAJOR 16: unregistered review claim and second-person voice

fixes.find: You want a written view on remaining life so you can budget, not a sales visit.
fixes.replace: A useful assessment gives a written view on remaining life for budgeting, not a sales pitch.
fixes.why: MAJOR 16: second-person voice

fixes.find: Matched replacement is not an upsell line. A new condenser on an old coil, or a two-stage furnace on a single-stage thermostat, gives you neither the efficiency nor the comfort on the label.
fixes.replace: Matched replacement is about performance, not an upsell. A new condenser needs a coil rated to pair with it on the same refrigerant, and multi-stage equipment needs a compatible control configured for its staging; otherwise the system may not deliver the efficiency or comfort on the label.
fixes.why: MAJOR 5/7: age alone does not decide mismatch; staging depends on configured control

fixes.find: Multi-stage equipment on a single-stage thermostat is money left on the table
fixes.replace: Multi-stage equipment needs a compatible, correctly configured control to deliver its rated staging
fixes.why: MAJOR 5: single-stage thermostat does not automatically disable staging

fixes.find: Replaced together, they match and stage properly
fixes.replace: Replaced together, they can be matched and staged as a rated pair
fixes.why: MAJOR 7: absolute matching claim
